{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "Original request S1–S10 and intake instructions",
    "README.md",
    "package.json",
    "src/server.js",
    "src/users.js",
    "src/paginate.js",
    "test/server.test.js",
    "test/users.test.js",
    "test/paginate.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the users API request, its constraints, and the decisions discovery must settle.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"id": "K1", "applies": "yes"},

    {"id": "K11", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K12", "applies": "yes"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Which clients use the users API, and how should they observe a successful create or careful delete?",
      "changes": "Consumer-facing workflow and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume HTTP API callers use the existing server; verify mutations through subsequent GET requests.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect available client and API documentation; otherwise nothing blocks proceeding with the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "How can optional pagination be exposed while preserving existing endpoint responses?",
      "changes": "List behavior, compatibility requirements and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve unparameterized GET /users as the existing array; introduce pagination only through an explicit request.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish existing clients and list contracts; incompatible changes to existing responses cannot proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What are the create, delete and pagination request fields, response bodies, status codes and errors, including what 'same shape' means for mutation responses?",
      "changes": "HTTP contracts and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use existing user objects with numeric id, name and email, and preserve existing GET response shapes; treat exact new contracts as provisional.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first check repository and client conventions and resolve Q2; finalizing new HTTP contracts depends on those findings."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What confirmation or other safeguard makes deletion careful, and how should missing, malformed or repeated deletion requests behave?",
      "changes": "Delete workflow, error behavior and safety tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume an explicit confirmation is required before deleting one identified user; do not delete on malformed, absent or unconfirmed requests.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first check existing client and product conventions; the final safeguard and its contract remain provisional without evidence or an owner decision."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What page size and page-boundary behavior are intended, including empty and short final pages?",
      "changes": "Pagination defaults and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use size 3 provisionally, as in the existing paginator test, and retain its one-based pages; fix the short-last-page calculation.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first look for client or product conventions; nothing blocks proceeding with the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Where should durable user data live, how should it initialize, and how are writes, concurrent changes, failures and restarts handled while retaining the in-memory store?",
      "changes": "Persistence design, configuration, failure handling and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume one server process with an in-memory working store backed by a local durable file, seeded only when no saved data exists; do not claim multi-process coordination.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the runtime filesystem, writable location and existing deployment conventions; a durable storage design cannot be finalized without them."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Who can create, list and delete users, how are callers identified, and what user data must be hidden from whom?",
      "changes": "Access rules, data exposure and security tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume the existing unauthenticated single-service API and existing visible user fields; no roles, sessions or privacy boundaries are implied.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect deployment and client context; nothing blocks the default, but it rules out claims of authenticated or per-user isolation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Does the target runtime provide Node 20 or later, a writable persistent location and the existing port configuration?",
      "changes": "Runtime setup, persistence viability and delivery checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node 20 or later, built-in modules only, and PORT with fallback 3000; assume no additional dependency.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect the intended runtime and storage access; deployment cannot be verified until those are known."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "What seams allow HTTP handling, in-memory state and persistence to be exercised independently without changing existing exports or responses unnecessarily?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and test isolation.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Retain the existing server, users and paginator modules and add only the smallest necessary persistence seam.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect existing module consumers and settle the persistence contract; nothing blocks provisional design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests demonstrate the HTTP contracts, short final page, safe deletion, persistence across restart and unchanged existing behavior?",
      "changes": "Verification coverage and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use node:test via npm test, with HTTP boundary and restart checks in addition to focused unit tests.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first settle the contracts and storage assumptions; final verification depends on their implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Is the named repository checkout the complete delivery target, or is there an identified deployment environment and release authority?",
      "changes": "Delivery steps and access requirements.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the result in this repository; no deployment target or release authority is specified.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect workspace delivery instructions; a deployed outcome cannot be claimed without an identified target, access and release."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Are there specific security, durability, performance or concurrency bounds beyond the existing service and careful deletion?",
      "changes": "Operational guarantees and acceptance tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the existing simple service model, validate destructive input and avoid claiming unrequested performance or multi-process guarantees.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect deployment and product requirements; nothing blocks the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "What evidence would expose data loss, unintended deletion, broken existing clients or incompatible migration IDs before delivery?",
      "changes": "Risk-focused checks and release acceptance.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Exercise restart persistence, deletion safeguards, existing GET responses, pagination boundaries and ID compatibility.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the migration contract and API behavior; migration compatibility cannot be verified without its authoritative constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What is the Kestrel migration's authoritative user ID format, allocation and uniqueness policy, and are existing numeric IDs required to remain unchanged?",
      "changes": "ID generation, persistence, migration compatibility tests and delivery acceptance.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Preserve existing numeric IDs and never intentionally reuse them; this is provisional and does not establish Kestrel compatibility.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first locate the migration specification or owner through authorized workspace sources; verified migration alignment and final acceptance remain open if no authoritative evidence is available."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What do the available improve and code-review workflows require, and how should parallel handler and test work be coordinated?",
      "changes": "Execution, review and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host-described improve loop until a pass finds only trivial changes, parallelize independent handler and test work, and perform code review before completion.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect the applicable installed workflow instructions and available worker capabilities; those later delivery steps cannot be claimed complete at intake."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the Node users API in this folder. S2 [outcome]: Add creation and safeguarded deletion for API callers; the confirmation contract remains open under Q3–Q4. S3 [outcome]: Support existing-style pagination with a usual-size default and verify the short final page; [fact] the paginator currently uses floor division and omits a partial last page, and [assumption] size 3 is provisional under Q5. S4 [boundary]: Keep the implementation simple and dependency-free. S5 [outcome]: Preserve users across restarts while retaining in-memory state; storage and concurrency assumptions are recorded in Q6. S6 [boundary]: Later work must run improve to its stopping condition, fan out handler and test work in parallel, and complete code review; workflow details are open under Q15. S7 [outcome]: Keep IDs aligned with the future Kestrel migration; [assumption] preserve current numeric IDs and avoid reuse, while Q14 must establish the authoritative migration contract. S8 [fact]: The existing server uses PORT or defaults to 3000. S9 [outcome]: Use the existing list shape where applicable; [fact] GET /users currently returns an array of user objects, and the new response contract is open under Q3. S10 [boundary]: Preserve existing endpoint returns, including the unparameterized list and individual-user responses; Q2 addresses pagination compatibility. [Fact] This intake is read-only, starts no server, implements nothing and authorizes no release; the named repository is the assumed delivery target, an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and a deployed outcome exists only after release. [Assumption] API callers share one service-level store across requests and sessions, durable until changed or removed; the current server has no caller identity or access controls, so Q6–Q7 cover lifetime, concurrent access and visibility. [Discovery leads, not verified facts]: inspect repository documentation, tests and applicable workflow instructions; look for Kestrel migration documentation, its team or owner, relevant workspace channels, internal sites and authorized private repositories; no particular locator or owner is established. Store any sensitive locator only in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/. No prior run is identified."
}
